The Petitioners have filed this petition against Respondents for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989.

2. The brief facts of case is as under:

sentences.text: That on 18.12.2019 at about 6.30 p.m. P.Sheik Abdul had been riding motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04- SCCH 5 Y-9588 at Chikkaballapura NH-44, BB Road, infront of BEML showroom, Chikkaballapura, at that time, another motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-E-2585 ridden by its rider at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against his motor cycle, as a result, P.Sheik Abdul fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, he was taken to Jeevan Hospital, Chikkaballapura, wherein Doctors have declared that, he was died on the way to the hospital.

Thereafter postmortem was conducted at Chikkaballapura Government Hospital and petitioners have performed funeral and obsequies ceremony by spending Rs.1,00,000/-, further they have also spent Rs.50,000/-
towards transportation of dead body.

3. At the time of accident, deceased was aged about 35 years, working as Technician Service (Automobile Engineer) at Bimal Auto Agency India (P) SCCH 5 Ltd., thereby earning Rs.20,890/-
p.m.

entities.text: Bimal Auto Agency India (P) SCCH 5 Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are minor children, petitioner No.3 is father and petitioner No.4 is mother of the deceased/P.Sheik Abdul, due to sudden demise of the deceased, he has left behind his beloved wife, minor children and his aged parents and petitioners have also lost his love and affection.

Out of the said accident, crime No.77/2019 is registered against the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-E-2585 before the Chikkaballapura Traffic Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 304(A) of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is previous R.C.Owner of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-E-2585 and respondent No.2 is insurer.
Petition against respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 is deleted.
Respondent No.3 is R.C.Owner and respondent No.4 is present R.C.Owner, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
So that, prays SCCH 5 to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.40,00,000/-.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/previous R.C.Owner of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-E-2585 has appeared, but not chosen to file written statement.
Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.
Further submitted that, there is delay of one day in lodging the complaint.

Further submitted that,
as per the claim petition, the validity period of insurance for the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-Y-9588 is mentioned as 25.05.2014 to 24.05.2015 and the date of accident is 18.12.2019, this shows that, motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-Y-9588 was not covered by insurance.
Further petitioners have not made owner and insurer of the said motor cycle as parties to the petition and respondent No.1 was not the owner of the said motor SCCH 5 cycle.

Further submitted that, police have filed charge sheet against the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-E-2585 namely Rajashekar S/o. Narayanaswamy under Sec.279, 337, 304(A) of IPC,
Sec.185, 181, 196 of M.V.Act and the said charge sheet rider was not having driving license, policy for motor cycle and moreover he had consumed alcohol and if any compensation is to be paid, it is to be paid by the owner of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-E-2585.
The riders of both the motor cycle were not having DL, policy for motor cycle and both the riders were not wearing helmet, hence petition is liable to be dismissed.
There is no compliance of Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

Ayisha Bhanu vs Raghunandan.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98260944/
3 5.
Respondent No.3/ R.C.Owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-E-2585 has appeared and SCCH 5 filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.

Respondent submitted that, he was R.C.Owner of the RX Yamaha bike bearing Reg.No.KA-40-E-2585 and later he has sold that vehicle for valuable consideration in favour of C.K.Gopinatha @ C.K.Gopiatha Naidu and hand over all the original documents like RC, insurance and executed Form No.29 and 30 to transfer the vehicle in his name.
Further submitted that, after purchase of the bike one C.K.Gopinath @ C.K.Gopinath Naidu was the absolute owner in possession of the bike bearing Reg.No.KA-40-E-2585.
Later inturn he has sold that bike in favour of Manjunath @ Malluri.

The said C.K.Gopinath has given statement before the police, as such he was deposed in his evidence before the Hon'ble Prl. Civil Judge and JMFC at Chikkaballapur in CC No.325/2020 that, he was purchased the Bike bearing Reg.No.KA-40-E-2585 Yamaha RX 100 on 21.06.2001 SCCH 5 from respondent No.3 and he has used said bike for the period of one month without transferring the RC with respect to the bike, after that he has sold the same in favour of Manjunath.

6. Further submitted that, above said Manjunath has sold the above vehicle in favour of K.R.Deepak,
as such Deepak is the absolute owner in possession and enjoyment of the vehicle and he is using that vehicle for his personal works.
He has handed over the bike in favour of Rajashekar to get the medicines.
So that, K.R.Deepak and Rajashekar having bound duty to pay any compensation.

Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
7.
Respondent No.4 has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.

He is owner of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-E- 2585 and policy was in force as on the date of accident SCCH 5 and submitted that, petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder such as owner and insurer of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-E-2585.
Further denies for having insured motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-Y-9588, also denies age, occupation and income of the deceased.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.

Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
8.

On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Late.P.Sheik Abdul, S/o.
Pyaru Sabi died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 18.12.2019 at about 6.30 p.m. near B.B.Road, in front of BEMIL Showroom, Chikkaballapura, due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-E-2585 by its rider, as mentioned in claim petition?
SCCH 5 2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or award?
Ayisha Bhanu vs Raghunandan.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98260944/
4 9.

In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 /wife of the deceased has deposed her evidence as PW-1, Manager in BIMAL Auto Agency is examined as PW-2 and marked 16 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16 and closed her evidence.
On the other hand, one K.Suryanarayana i.e., respondent No.3 is examined as RW-1 and marked documents as per Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.9.
Further one C.K.Gopinath is examined as RW-2 and closed his evidence.
10. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record.

Then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  SCCH 5  Issue No.3 :
As per final order for the  following:
: : REASONS::
11. Issue No.1:- In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1/wife of the deceased has deposed her evidence as PW-1, in her chief-examination she has reiterated the facts narrated in their petition.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of P.M.Report is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of inquest mahazar is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.7 and copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.8.
12.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and the records those have marked i.e., FIR, complaint,
P.M.Report, mahazar, inquest mahazar, sketch, IMV SCCH 5 Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioners about causing of the accident dated 18.12.2019 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
13.

On the other hand, R.C.Holder of the vehicle RX-Yamaha bike bearing Reg.No.KA-40-E-2585 is examined as RW-1 and he has furnished copy of order sheet in CC No.325/2020 JMFC,
Chikkaballapura marked as Ex.R.1, copy of complaint marked as Ex.R.2, copy of FIR marked as Ex.R.3, copy of spot mahazar marked as Ex.R.4, copy of statements of Suryanarayana, Gopiath Naidu, Manjunath @ Malluri and Deepak marked as Ex.R.5 to Ex.R.8 and copy of statement of delivery note marked as Ex.R.9.

The previous owner who in possession of the bike bearing Reg.No.KA-40-E-2585 by name C.K.Gopinath @ C.K.Gopinath Naidu is examined as RW-2.
SCCH 5 14.

But none of the respondents documents and evidence of RW-1 and RW-2 have support their case Ayisha Bhanu vs Raghunandan.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98260944/
5 about non causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

sentences.text: Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioners about death of Sheik Abudl out of the accident held on 18.12.2019 at about 6.30 p.m. while he was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-Y-9588 at Chikkaballapura, NH-Bb road, infront of BEMIL Show room, Chikkaballapura.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioners.
15. The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-E-2585.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioners, this tribunal SCCH 5 comes to the conclusion that, petitioners have proved the above issue No.1 in their favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

16. Issue No.2:- As per the case of the petitioners, deceased/P.Sheik Abdul was aged about 35 years as on the date of accident, for proof of age of the deceased, copy of aadhar card of the deceased is on record, wherein date of birth is mentioned as 09.10.1983, the alleged accident was occurred on 18.12.2019.

Accordingly relying on copy of aadhar card of the deceased, age of the deceased is considered about 37 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 15 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. As per the case of the petitioners, deceased was working as Head Mechanic in Bimal Auto Agency, SCCH 5 thereby drawing salary of Rs.20,890/- p.m.
In this regard, petitioners have exhibited copy of salary slip of the deceased marked as Ex.P.15.
In support of their case, Manager in Bimal Auto Agency is examined as PW-2 and he has exhibited salary slips marked as Ex.P.16.
So as per the evidence of PW-2 and Ex.P.16 salary slips, I have no hesitation to take monthly income of the deceased as Rs.17,424/- p.m. i.e., last salary of the deceased.

". 
The said admissions of PW-2 have not supports the respondent No.3 case in any manner.
So as per the evidence of PW-1 and Ex.P.16 salary slips, I have no hesitation to take monthly income of the deceased as Rs.17,424/- p.m. i.e., last salary of the deceased.
SCCH 5 18.

Further petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioner No.2 is minor son, petitioner No.3 is minor daughter,
petitioner No.4 is father and petitioner No.5 is mother of the deceased/P.Sheik Abdul.

To prove the said facts, they have furnished notarized copy of aadhar cards of petitioner No.1 to 5 are marked as Ex.P.9 to 13 it reveals that, they are legal representatives of the deceased P.Sheik Abdul, hence they will become dependents of the deceased.

Ayisha Bhanu vs Raghunandan.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98260944/
6 19.

As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the number of dependents are 4 to 6, then 1/4th of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/4th of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

20. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, The Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear SCCH 5 that, an addition of 40% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged upto 40 years, in case of self employed person or person having fixed salary as future prospects.

National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand, the monthly income of the deceased is taken as Rs.17,424/- hence, which is taken for additional weightage at the rate of 40% with reference to his age.
21. Hence, the following calculation is made for loss of dependency.

Sl. Particulars Calculation Total No.
 (i) Monthly Income Rs.17,424/-
(ii) 40% of (i) above if Rs.17,424/- (+) added to the Rs.6,970/- = monthly income as Rs.24,394/-
future prospects (iii) 1/4th of (ii) of the Rs.24,394/- (-) same to be deducted Rs.6,098/- = towards personal and living expenses Monthly income Rs.18,296/-
SCCH 5 (iv) Compensation after Rs.18,296/- x Rs.32,93,280/-
multiplier of 15 is 12 x 15 applied 22.
Further petitioner No.1 being the wife of the deceased is entitled for Rs.20,000/- towards consortium.

Petitioner No.2 and 3 being minor children of the deceased are entitled for Rs.20,000/-
each towards loss of parental consortium and petitioner No.4 and 5 being parents of the defendant are entitled for Rs.20,000/- each towards filial consortium.
Further they are entitled for loss of estate of Rs.15,000/- and also they are entitled for funeral expenses for an amount of Rs.15,000/-.

23. The details of compensation awarded is as under:
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs.
1. Loss of dependency 32,93,280-00 2.
Loss of consortium 20,000-00 (Petitioner No.1) SCCH 5 Ayisha Bhanu vs Raghunandan.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98260944/

7 3. Loss of parental consortium 40,000-00 (Rs.20,000/- each to Petitioner No.2 and 3)
4. Loss of filial consortium 40,000-00 (Rs.20,000/- each to Petitioner No.4 and 5)
4. Loss of Estate 15,000-00 5. Funeral Expenses 15,000-00 Total 34,23,280-00 24.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.34,23,280/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

25. Further in the entire case proceedings, respondent No.3 has taken contention that, after purchase of the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-E-2585 i.e., offending vehicle, immediately he sold the same to one C.K.Gopinatha @ C.K.Gopinatha Naidu.
He also executed Form No.29 and 30 in favour of him including SCCH 5 delivery note etc.,
Ofcourse to substantiate the said facts, he has exhibited Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.9 documents out of them Ex.R.9 is is the significant document i.e., Delivery Note.

As per the said document, he has executed delivery note dated 21.06.2001, but admittedly the said vehicle i.e., offending vehicle has not been transferred either in the name of RW-2 C.K.Gopinath nor any other persons, but for the date of the alleged accident dated 18.12.2019, the offending vehicle stood in the name of respondent No.3 K.Suryanarayana.
The said fact has not disputed on both sides, that means the offending vehicle stood in the name of respondent No.3 for the date of alleged accident is not at all disputed.

Further admittedly for the the date of the alleged accident, there is no insurance policy to the offending vehicle, as such respondent No.2 Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., has been deleted from the cause title of the petition.
SCCH 5 26.

Further during the course of arguments, the learned counsel for respondent No.3 Sri.M.R.
vehemently argued that, insurance policy of the offending vehicle has been lapsed and the vehicle was sold by respondent No.3 to one C.K.Gopinatha and the said C.K.Gopinatha has not obtained RC in his name and inturn he has sold the vehicle to one Manjunath @ Malluri and deceased has not having valid driving license and not produced the same and there is no documents for the avocation of the deceased and no salary slips has been produced and in the year 2001 itself the delivery note has been executed by the respondent No.3 and respondent No.3 is not liable for the alleged accident and compensation etc.,

But inview of the aforesaid reasons, the oral evidence of RW-2 and other evidence placed by respondent No.3 have not sufficient to disbelieve the case of the petitioner about non-liability of respondent No.3 to pay SCCH 5 compensation to the legal heirs of the deceased.

As stated supra, there is no dispute with regard to expiry of the insurance policy for the date of the alleged accident for the offending vehicle of the respondent No.3 bearing Reg.No.KA-40-E-2585.
27.

Ofcourse respondent No.3 has taken some independent contention as stated supra, but admittedly the charge sheet and other materials clearly indicates to the court that, for the date of the alleged accident, respondent No.3 is R.C.Owner of the alleged offending vehicle and admittedly Ayisha Bhanu vs Raghunandan.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98260944/
8 charge sheet is also filed by the police against one Rajashekar N.
So inview of the said reasons any of the arguments addressed by the respondent No.3 counsel have not supports this case in any manner.
Accordingly respondent No.3 is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With SCCH 5 these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
28. Issue No.3:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.34,23,280/- (Rupees Thirty Four Lakhs Twenty Three Thousand Two Hundred Eighty Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.3 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio 60:10:10:10:10 in the award amount.
SCCH 5 The petitioners No.1, 4 and 5 are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
Since Petitioner No.2 and 3 are minors, on deposit of the award amount, entire share shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank till he attains age of majority with a liberty to draw accrued interest in the name of minor Petitioner guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor Petitioners.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.issue:
On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Late.P.Sheik Abdul, S/o.
Pyaru Sabi died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 18.12.2019 at about 6.30 p.m. near B.B.Road, in front of BEMIL Showroom, Chikkaballapura, due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-E-2585 by its rider, as mentioned in claim petition?
SCCH 5 2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Accordingly relying on copy of aadhar card of the deceased, age of the deceased is considered about 37 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 15 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.
20. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, The Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear SCCH 5 that, an addition of 40% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged upto 40 years, in case of self employed person or person having fixed salary as future prospects.
In the case on hand, the monthly income of the deceased is taken as Rs.17,424/- hence, which is taken for additional weightage at the rate of 40% with reference to his age.
The said fact has not disputed on both sides, that means the offending vehicle stood in the name of respondent No.3 for the date of alleged accident is not at all disputed.
Further admittedly for the the date of the alleged accident, there is no insurance policy to the offending vehicle, as such respondent No.2 Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., has been deleted from the cause title of the petition.
But inview of the aforesaid reasons, the oral evidence of RW-2 and other evidence placed by respondent No.3 have not sufficient to disbelieve the case of the petitioner about non-liability of respondent No.3 to pay SCCH 5 compensation to the legal heirs of the deceased.

::ORDER::
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.34,23,280/- (Rupees Thirty Four Lakhs Twenty Three Thousand Two Hundred Eighty Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.3 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio 60:10:10:10:10 in the award amount.
SCCH 5 The petitioners No.1, 4 and 5 are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
Since Petitioner No.2 and 3 are minors, on deposit of the award amount, entire share shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank till he attains age of majority with a liberty to draw accrued interest in the name of minor Petitioner guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor Petitioners.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
